message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI

on:
  push:
    paths-ignore:
      - .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**
      - doc/**
      - man/**
      - '**/LICENCE'
      - '**/.gitignore'
      - '**.md'
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**
      - doc/**
      - man/**
      - '**/LICENCE'
      - '**/.gitignore'
      - '**.md'
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        cxx: [g++, clang++]
        libc: [glibc]
        include:
          - cxx: g++
            cc: gcc
          - cxx: clang++
            cc: clang
          - libc: glibc
            shell: bash

    defaults:
      run:
        shell: ${{ matrix.shell }}

    steps:
      - name: Set up Ubuntu
        if: matrix.libc == 'glibc'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y autopoint pkgconf gettext libcamera-dev libopencv-dev libavcodec-dev libavdevice-dev libavformat-dev libavutil-dev libswscale-dev libwebp-dev libmicrohttpd-dev libmariadb-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libfftw3-dev

      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@main

      - name: Configure build
        run: |
          autoreconf -fiv
          ./configure CC=${{ matrix.cc }} CXX=${{ matrix.cxx }}

      - name: Build target
        run: |
          ${{ matrix.CXX }} --version
          make -j $(($(nproc)+1))

      - name: Run artifact
        run: |
          file ./src/motion
          ./src/motion -h || true",
  "rationale": "The build job has no explicit timeout, so a hung or runaway job can consume the default 360-minute runner budget. Evidence pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) supports adding an explicit job budget to reduce runaway consumption, with reported VM-time reduction for free runners. The change is minimal: add timeout-minutes: 60 to the build job. All build/test steps, the matrix (g++/clang++ over glibc), fail-fast: false, path filters, and concurrency cancellation are preserved, so intended coverage and required-check semantics are unchanged. Historical CI runs show successful completions well under this bound (the slowest success is about 15 minutes), giving operational headroom for cold dependency installation without risking false timeouts on valid runs. No new network access, secrets, privileged actions, publishing, or deployment operations are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
